title: Trump DOJ Appointee Who Led ‘Grand Conspiracy’ Probe Resigns, Sparking Political Fallout
body:
WASHINGTON — The Justice Department’s senior official who oversaw the controversial “grand conspiracy” probe into former President Donald Trump’s critics has tendered his resignation, ending a tenure that has been marked by intense political scrutiny and accusations of partisan overreach. The departure of Michael G. Hernandez, a Trump‑appointed senior counsel to the Office of the Attorney General, comes as the investigation—launched in 2022 to examine alleged collusion among federal law‑enforcement officials during prior inquiries into the former president—faces mounting pressure from both Congress and the White House to wind down.

Hernandez, who joined the Department of Justice in the final months of the Trump administration, was tasked with leading a team of attorneys and investigators tasked with uncovering what they described as a “coordinated effort” by the FBI, the Department of Homeland Security and other agencies to undermine Trump’s political agenda. Critics, however, have labeled the inquiry a “grand conspiracy” chase, arguing that it was designed more to intimidate political opponents than to uncover genuine wrongdoing. Over the past two years, the probe has produced few substantive findings, and its budgetary demands have drawn fire from lawmakers who question the allocation of federal resources to a politically charged investigation.

The resignation, submitted last week, was accepted by Acting Attorney General Lisa Monroe, who praised Hernandez’s “dedication to public service” while noting that the Department will conduct a thorough review of the office’s ongoing work. In a brief statement, Hernandez said his decision was “motivated by a desire to allow the Department to refocus its priorities on matters of pressing national importance.” The timing of his exit is notable: it coincides with a broader DOJ effort to recalibrate its investigative agenda after the 2024 midterm elections, during which both parties have called for greater transparency and depoliticization of federal law‑enforcement operations.

Political analysts view the resignation as a signal that the Trump‑era initiative to scrutinize law‑enforcement officials may be losing steam. “The grand conspiracy narrative has been a rallying point for a segment of the former president’s base, but it has not yielded the concrete evidence needed to sustain a lasting legal campaign,” said Dr. Elena Ramirez, a professor of political science at Georgetown University. “Hernandez’s departure could indicate that the Department is acknowledging the limited utility of the probe and is shifting resources toward more traditional criminal and civil enforcement priorities.”

Congressional oversight committees have already begun hearings to assess the scope and impact of the investigation. Republican members have defended the probe as a necessary check on potential abuse of power, while Democrats have urged the DOJ to terminate the effort, calling it a “political witch hunt” that undermines public confidence in the justice system. The House Judiciary Committee is expected to issue a subpoena next month for documents related to the grand conspiracy inquiry, a move that could further pressure the DOJ to close the file.

Looking ahead, the resignation may pave the way for a restructuring of the DOJ’s internal oversight mechanisms. Acting Attorney General Monroe has indicated that the Department will appoint an interim head to manage the remaining aspects of the investigation while a permanent replacement is sought. Observers suggest that the new leadership will likely emphasize impartiality and adherence to established investigative protocols, aiming to restore credibility after a period of heightened partisanship. As the DOJ navigates this transition, the broader implications for the relationship between the Justice Department and political actors remain uncertain, but the exit of Hernandez marks a decisive step toward recalibrating the agency’s focus in a post‑Trump political landscape.
